high.title: Bursa ends lower ahead of Fed decision, tech earnings
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the FOMC interest rate decision and major US tech earnings releases. Concerns over Nvidia's AI financing commitments exceeding US$750 billion raised questions about the sustainability of AI-driven demand, weighing on sentiment. Falling Brent crude prices of over 2% also failed to lift market mood as regional markets weakened.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher against most currencies, slips versus US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit slipped against the US dollar to 4.0885/4.0930 as markets awaited the FOMC meeting outcome and its guidance on US interest rates. Declining global crude oil prices, driven by US-Iran negotiations and hopes of easing West Asia tensions, added further pressure on the ringgit-dollar pair. The currency's performance is closely tied to Fed policy signals, making this a key watchpoint for Malaysian investors.

high.title: Ringgit strengthens ahead of US Fed rate decision
high.summary: The ringgit climbed to 4.0835/4.0875 against the USD as markets await the FOMC meeting on July 28-29, which could signal a rate hike supporting the US dollar. Crude oil prices fell sharply following a US-Iran hostilities pause, with WTI dropping 6.98% and Brent falling 7.94%. These dual forces — geopolitical easing and Fed policy uncertainty — are critical drivers for Malaysian currency and market sentiment.

high.title: Oil prices sink as US-Iran pause fuels fresh Hormuz hopes
high.summary: Brent crude broke above US$100/barrel last week due to US-Iran conflict escalation affecting the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping lanes, before retreating sharply on ceasefire hopes. The easing of tensions in these critical energy corridors has significant implications for global oil supply and inflation outlooks. As an oil-exporting nation, Malaysia's fiscal position and energy-linked stocks are directly impacted by these price swings.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on bargain hunting
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia rebounded as easing West Asia tensions drove Brent crude down nearly 8%, alleviating inflation concerns and prompting investors to rotate back into risk assets. Rakuten Trade maintains a cautious near-term outlook as markets await US Fed policy decisions and major tech earnings. The interplay between geopolitical developments, oil prices, and Fed policy represents a high-impact environment for Malaysian equities.

high.title: Bursa retreats as market digests latest US tariffs
high.summary: The FBM KLCI faced selling pressure as US tariffs, surging Brent crude above US$100/barrel, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East dampened market sentiment. Attacks on Saudi oil tankers and US strikes on Iran have intensified supply concerns, pushing oil prices higher and threatening global inflation. The 1,700 level is seen as key technical support amid the current market pullback.

high.title: Ringgit ends slightly lower amid Middle East tensions, US tariffs
high.summary: The ringgit weakened against the US dollar as a new 10% forced labour-related tariff on Malaysian exports to the US took effect, adding pressure alongside Middle East geopolitical risks. The Strait of Hormuz blockade is pushing crude oil prices higher, increasing demand for safe-haven US dollars. Malaysia's MITI has confirmed ongoing engagement with the US to address the tariff issue.

high.title: Bursa opens lower amid cautious market sentiment
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened in negative territory with the FBM KLCI dropping over 6 points as Brent crude surpassed US$100/barrel and Wall Street's Nasdaq fell 2.15% following disappointing reactions to Alphabet's and Tesla's spending plans. Losers significantly outpaced gainers in early trade, reflecting broad-based risk aversion. The confluence of high energy prices and US tech sector weakness signals heightened near-term volatility for local equities.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, softer vs US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit weakened against the US dollar to 4.0925/4.0980 following Trump's announcement of additional import tariffs of 10%-12.5% on 60 economies including Malaysia, citing forced labour practices. This marks a significant policy escalation after the US Supreme Court annulled previous tariff measures, with the ringgit expected to trade cautiously in the RM4.08-RM4.10 range. Malaysian businesses and investors face heightened trade uncertainty as new tariff pressures weigh on the local currency.

high.title: Ringgit ends lower amid Middle East tensions
high.summary: The ringgit eased to 4.0870/4.0910 against the US dollar as escalating Middle East military conflicts drove Brent crude up 4.23% to US$98.05 per barrel, raising global oil supply concerns. The surge in oil prices has increased the odds of a US interest rate hike in September, strengthening the US dollar and pressuring emerging market currencies like the ringgit. Malaysian investors and businesses should monitor inflationary impacts and potential central bank policy responses globally.

medium.title: Kangaroo market is now the new normal
medium.summary: JF Apex Securities has characterised the current market environment as a 'Kangaroo market' marked by rapid, directionless swings driven by multiple simultaneous geopolitical and policy catalysts. Investors face a complex landscape of Middle East tensions, shipping disruptions across key routes, Trump tariffs, uncertain Fed policy, and slowing Chinese demand. This headline-driven volatility is expected to persist for months, posing strategic challenges for Malaysian market participants.

medium.title: Bursa opens lower on cautious stance ahead of FOMC meeting
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened lower at 1,711.95 and fell further to 1,706.33 by 9.15am as cautious sentiment prevailed ahead of the FOMC decision. Losers significantly outpaced gainers with subdued turnover, reflecting a broad risk-off posture among investors. The market's muted opening signals that domestic trading activity is heavily influenced by external US monetary policy uncertainty.

medium.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, eases vs US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit opened slightly weaker against the US dollar at 4.0850/4.0900, with Bank Muamalat's chief economist noting elevated odds of a US interest rate rise supporting dollar strength. The currency is expected to trade in a narrow range as markets await the two-day FOMC meeting outcome. Malaysian businesses and investors with USD exposure should monitor the Fed's guidance closely for potential currency impact.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds at open as investors track pause in US airstrikes
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 2.05 points to 1,703.07 at the open, with gainers outpacing losers as easing geopolitical tensions and softer energy prices lifted sentiment. Malacca Securities noted the rebound follows last week's sell-off, with investors also positioning ahead of Big Tech earnings and the US Fed rate decision. This intraday update reflects improving but still cautious market conditions relevant to short-term traders.

medium.title: Ringgit rises against US dollar ahead of Negeri Sembilan poll
medium.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0830/4.0930 against the USD in early trading, with analysts watching whether the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election (polling Aug 1) could influence national political sentiment and currency support. External factors including the FOMC meeting and potential US rate hike continue to dominate, with the likelihood of a hike seen as supportive of the USD. Domestic political developments add a layer of uncertainty for ringgit-sensitive investments.

medium.title: Westports outperforms despite Middle East fallout
medium.summary: Westports delivered a strong Q2 FY2026 with net profit surging 56% year-on-year to RM360.9 million, beating analyst expectations despite a 40% spike in fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict. H1 FY2026 net profit rose 51% to RM687.4 million on revenue of RM1.76 billion, even as container volumes dipped 1%. Multiple research houses maintained 'buy' ratings, highlighting the company's resilience and operational efficiency.

medium.title: Khazanah said to sell US$340mil Tenaga stake in placement
medium.summary: Khazanah Nasional is reported to have sold 100 million Tenaga Nasional shares at RM13.91 each, a 4.5% discount to market price, raising approximately US$340 million in a block placement. This reduces Khazanah's stake in Tenaga and may signal a strategic portfolio rebalancing by the sovereign wealth fund. The placement could exert short-term pressure on Tenaga's share price while potentially improving liquidity and free float.
